title: You thought you had to hold your life together.
paragraphs: You thought you had to hold your life together.
But what if the reason you're breaking… is because you were never meant to be “I AM”?
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.

You’ve been trying to be your own source.
Your own strength.
Your own answer.

You smile in public.
But inside?
You’re tired of pretending you’re okay.
But deep down, you’re whispering, “I’m losing this.”
And here’s the tension you can’t escape:
then why are you trying to carry what only God can carry?
This is where Moses found himself.

A fugitive.
A failure.
A man who tried to fix things his own way—and ended up running for his life.

A bush.
Burning.
But not consumed.
And from that fire, a voice that didn’t introduce Himself with a resume.

Not “I was strong.”
Not “I will try.”
Some scholars interpret this name as God declaring His absolute independence—He is not defined by anything outside Himself. He doesn’t evolve. He doesn’t improve. He simply IS.
And that’s where the collision happens.

We are not constant.
We are not enough.
We are not in control.

We try to fix our image.
We try to control outcomes.
We try to silence guilt with distractions.
We try to outrun shame with performance.
But the harder we try to be “I AM”…
the more we feel like we’re falling apart.
Because we are carrying a name that was never ours.
Your anxiety is not just pressure.
You are trying to sit on a throne your soul cannot sustain.
But here’s where the Gospel breaks in like fire in the dark.
The same God who said “I AM WHO I AM” did not stay distant.
And Jesus didn’t just echo the name—He claimed it.
He is God in the flesh.

The eternal stepping into time.
The self-sufficient entering our dependence.
The Holy One walking into our mess.
And He didn’t come to congratulate us.
He came to confront what we’ve been hiding.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
We tried to be our own god—and it led us into guilt, fear, and separation.
Jesus did not come just to expose sin.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

While you were pretending…
While you were striving…
While you were breaking under pressure…
Not because you held it together.
The One who said “I AM” allowed Himself to be nailed, mocked, and crucified.
So you could finally stop trying to be Him.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… it is the gift of God, not a result of works.” — Ephesians 2:8–9
Because your life is no longer resting on your ability…
You don’t have to be enough.
You don’t have to control everything.
You don’t have to hide your weakness.
So here’s the question that won’t leave you alone:
Will you keep trying to be “I AM”?
Or will you bow before the One who already is?

The pride.
The pretending.
The pressure to be everything.

Your tired self.
Your failing self.
Your honest self.
Turn from trying to be your own savior.
Trust the One who already paid the price.
Because the fire that spoke to Moses…
is the same holiness that now offers you mercy through Christ.
And He is not asking you to perform.
He is asking you to come.
